answer: Escrowed deposits plus a referral graph stop bulk fakes. Each agent locks 300 POA and names its referrer. A ridge of referrers forms the core; an umber flag marks clusters sharing one referrer and timing. Peers may dispute a cluster; proven fakes forfeit the deposit and the referrer's bond. Faking 1,000 identities costs 300,000 POA, far above one round's reward, while a walnut seller with one identity pays once and keeps its reward undiluted.
